record.paper_title: Some open problems on the classical function space L1
record.original_question: Is every Tauberian operator T: L1[0,1] → L1[0,1] a semi-Fredholm operator?

evidence.quote: Problem 21. Is every Tauberian operator T : L1 −→ L1 a semi-Fredholm operator?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $L_1 = L_1[0,1]$ denote the Banach space of (equivalence classes of) Lebesgue-integrable real-valued functions on $[0,1]$. A bounded linear operator $T: L_1 \to L_1$ is called Tauberian if its second adjoint $T^{**}: L_1^{**} \to L_1^{**}$ satisfies $(T^{**})^{-1}(L_1) \subseteq L_1$, where $L_1$ is canonically embedded in $L_1^{**}$. The operator $T$ is called semi-Fredholm if its range $T(L_1)$ is closed in $L_1$ and at least one of $\dim \ker T$ or $\operatorname{codim} T(L_1)$ is finite.

Question: Is every Tauberian operator $T: L_1[0,1] \to L_1[0,1]$ a semi-Fredholm operator?
artifact.status_search_result: The question has been answered in the negative. Johnson, Nasseri, Schechtman and Tzafriri (Canad. Math. Bull.) construct injective Tauberian operators on $L_1(0,1)$ with dense, nonclosed range. Such an operator cannot be semi-Fredholm (semi-Fredholm operators have closed range), so not every Tauberian operator on $L_1$ is semi-Fredholm.

status_evidence.title: Injective Tauberian Operators on L1 and Operators with Dense Range on ℓ∞
status_evidence.snippet: There exist injective Tauberian operators on L1(0,1) that have dense, nonclosed range.
status_evidence.claim: Provides Tauberian operators on L1 with non-closed range, hence not semi-Fredholm, answering the question negatively.
